title: Wet Paint
teaser: A brass plaque vanished from the town fountain overnight. Somebody ignored the sign.

booklet.briefing:
Pennick's Founders' Fountain has carried a brass plaque since 1902. It is fixed with four screws to the stone pillar, high above head height.

On Thursday evening a council painter gave the bench beside the fountain a fresh coat of green paint. On Friday at dawn the street sweeper found the four screws on the ground and the plaque gone.

Scrap brass sells well, and antique brass sells even better. Three people had reasons to be in the square. Find the one who left their mark.
rules: The plaque was stolen between 9:00 pm Thursday and 6:00 am Friday.

suspects.name: Gus Ferreira
suspects.description: Painted the bench on Thursday evening. Green paint all over his overalls.
suspects.statement: I painted the bench from six until half six, put my Wet Paint sign up and went home. I never touched the plaque.

suspects.name: Dana Whitlock
suspects.description: Runs the shop on the corner of the square. Offered the council money for the plaque last year and was turned down.
suspects.motive: Wanted the plaque for her shop window.
suspects.statement: Yes, I wanted that plaque. I asked politely and they said no. I had supper at the café and went home before nine.

suspects.name: Corwin Mays
suspects.description: Drives a flatbed truck around town buying old metal. Tall, wears heavy work boots.
suspects.motive: Brass fetches a high price at the scrapyard.
suspects.statement: I wasn't anywhere near the fountain last night. If there's paint on my boots, it's from home.

evidence.title: The fountain pillar
evidence.body:
Four empty screw holes. The bottom of the plaque's outline is 2.1 metres above the ground. Nobody can reach the top screws without standing on something.

The only thing within reach is the bench, pushed right up against the pillar.
lines: Four empty screw holes. The bottom of the plaque's outline is 2.1 metres above the ground. Nobody can reach the top screws without standing on something.
The only thing within reach is the bench, pushed right up against the pillar.

evidence.title: The bench seat
evidence.body:
The seat is made of four wooden slats with gaps between them.

Two boot prints are pressed into the paint on the seat, side by side, as if someone stood there facing the pillar.

Prints: size 11, a sole with straight ridges running across it.
lines: The seat is made of four wooden slats with gaps between them.

evidence.title: Label on the paint tin
evidence.body:
COUNCIL GREEN No. 4. Exterior wood paint.

Touch dry: 12 hours. Do not sit, lean or stand on surfaces before then.
lines: COUNCIL GREEN No. 4. Exterior wood paint.
Touch dry: 12 hours. Do not sit, lean or stand on surfaces before then.

evidence.title: Witness: café owner
evidence.body: “I locked up at nine o'clock sharp. The plaque was still on the fountain, I always look at it. Mrs. Whitlock paid for her supper at 8:40 and walked home up Hill Street.”
lines: “I locked up at nine o'clock sharp. The plaque was still on the fountain, I always look at it. Mrs. Whitlock paid for her supper at 8:40 and walked home up Hill Street.”

evidence.title: Footwear examination
evidence.body:
Each suspect's footwear from Thursday night was collected and examined.

Suspect | Shoes | Size | Sole | Paint found
Gus Ferreira | Canvas sneakers | 9 | Smooth rubber | Small green specks on the toes and laces only. Soles clean.
Dana Whitlock | Leather heels | 6 | Smooth leather | None.
Corwin Mays | Work boots | 11 | Straight ridges across the sole | Four green stripes across each sole, evenly spaced. Matches Council Green No. 4 and was still slightly tacky.
lines: Each suspect's footwear from Thursday night was collected and examined.

rows: Small green specks on the toes and laces only. Soles clean.
Four green stripes across each sole, evenly spaced. Matches Council Green No. 4 and was still slightly tacky.

evidence.title: Corwin's yard
evidence.body:
Corwin's shed door is painted dark brown. No green paint of any kind was found on his property.

Under a tarp on the flatbed truck: a screwdriver and a sack of mixed brass.
lines: Corwin's shed door is painted dark brown. No green paint of any kind was found on his property.

solution.explanation: Corwin Mays came to the square after the café shut, climbed onto the bench to reach the plaque and unscrewed it. He ignored the Wet Paint sign, and the bench printed four green stripes across his soles while he stood there. The plaque was in a sack of brass on his truck.

chain.step: The plaque is too high to reach without standing on the bench, which was still wet all night.
Size 11 prints with straight ridges were left in the paint on the seat.
Only Corwin's boots are size 11 with straight ridges, and they carry four fresh green stripes that match the four slats and Council Green No. 4.
He has no green paint at home, and brass and a screwdriver were on his truck.
